signals.thesis: Lam Research at $366.81 continues its breakout above the prior 52-week high. The semiconductor equipment complex is being re-rated as AI capex demand shows no signs of slowing — every fab expansion (TSMC, Samsung, Intel Foundry) requires LRCX etch and deposition tools. Volume at 9.0M is 3x average. RSI 68.5 leaves room before overbought territory. EMA20 ($316) well below price confirms the momentum. The entry at $358 on pullback from today's high gives a clean breakout continuation with stop below the prior resistance level.

ARM surged +11.3% to $380.81 on massive volume (16.3M vs avg) as AI chip design demand accelerated. The company's royalty model benefits from every major AI accelerator shipped globally — NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Apple, MediaTek all use ARM architecture. RSI 63.8 provides room to run before overextension. EMA20 well above EMA50 confirms strong momentum. Price above the 50-day average ($238) by 60% — a parabolic move that typically has follow-through in momentum regimes. Mega-cap ($407B) with regime oscillation advisory favoring large names.

GE Aerospace at $335.30 (+0.8%) is within 4% of its 52-week high ($348.48). The aerospace sector benefits from commercial aviation recovery and defense spending tailwinds. Volume at 2.9M is in line with average — steady institutional accumulation. RSI 63.0 is healthy. EMA20 ($302) confirms strong uptrend with price 11% above the 50-DMA. Entry at $330 on pullback gives a clean breakout setup with stop below the EMA20 level.

Caterpillar closed at $910.57 (+1.4%) near its 52-week high ($946.83). The construction and mining equipment giant benefits from the US infrastructure spending cycle, global re-industrialization, and copper/gold mining capex boom. RSI 54.6 is ideal — strong momentum without overextension. ATR $39 implies natural volatility, stop width $38 (4.2%) is appropriate at ~1.0x ATR. Copper surging +3.2% to $6.47/lb today provides a direct tailwind for mining equipment demand.
